pos.personaBrief: Boca chose when to attack, used long balls into the space between Geremi and Hierro and countered via Riquelme, yet Bianchi said his team managed the tempo and Riquelme kept the ball under control.

pro.personaBrief: Both Intercontinental goals came from long balls (Matellan to Delgado, Riquelme to Palermo) and recoveries went forward at once ('tac'), though Boca also built from the back at times.

est.personaBrief: A fixed 4-3-1-2 with defined roles (Battaglia and Basualdo winning the ball, Palermo as the box striker) with Riquelme free to roam.

lar.personaBrief: 4-3-1-2 with no wingers, attack through enganche Riquelme and two strikers, with full-backs Ibarra and Arruabarrena going forward only as support.

blo.personaBrief: Against Real Madrid Boca defended with nearly seven at the back, an offside trap and achique on free kicks, waiting rather than pressing high.

mar.personaBrief: Matellan was given personal marking of Figo and the team leaned on clear individual responsibilities, with a compact offside-trap defence.

pla.personaBrief: Bianchi said he defined systems according to players and situations, dropped Fagiani for Matellan to mark Figo, and made a tactical second-half adjustment against Real Madrid.

res.personaBrief: Pragmatic winner of Libertadores and Intercontinental, with a defensive block shutting the game down and intelligence over flourish.

sis.personaBrief: Bianchi wanted good, intelligent players with a drilled plan, gave Riquelme freedom to roam but kept collective discipline for all.

jog.personaBrief: Built around the classic number 10 Riquelme, with technical midfielders who also recovered the ball, and strong defenders winning duels.

bas.personaBrief: Squad of experienced signings (Basualdo, Bermudez, Palermo), with more than 20 starters, and few youngsters used only occasionally.

lid.personaBrief: Bianchi stated that all decisions were his and the group came first, with squad harmony built on listening and working.
